source_access: Cached abstracts for these nine inherited primary citations; separate newer sources and gene consultations retain their own access scopes.

references.10544286: Reporter-ferredoxin coexpression identifies component requirements under that experimental regime; it does not establish universal native essentiality.
references.10869428: E. coli IscU and HscB form a complex and synergistically stimulate HscA ATPase activity, connecting specific scaffold recruitment to the dedicated ATPase cycle.
references.11319236: Purified E. coli holo-IscA supports formation of holoferredoxin; this is cluster-transfer evidence distinct from iron donation.
references.11432781: Native E. coli genetic tests identify strong IscS/IscU/HscBA/Fdx effects and a smaller IscA effect in the tested background, without extending dispensability across conditions.
references.11577100: Radiotracer and binding measurements support direct E. coli IscS-to-IscU sulfur transfer; disruption of the donor-acceptor interface reduces transfer despite retained desulfurase activity.
references.15247288: E. coli IscA supports iron delivery to IscU when citrate limits free iron in vitro; native iron-source identity remains unresolved.
references.15485839: E. coli IscU and HscB synergistically accelerate the HscA ATPase cycle and scaffold capture; this does not by itself demonstrate generic protein folding.
references.15964837: Purified E. coli IscU and IscA support repeated cluster formation/transfer to apoferredoxin, providing activity evidence beyond static binding.
references.23682711: Reduced E. coli Fdx supplies electrons during IscS cysteine turnover; binding competition in this assay does not establish one invariant complex architecture under all conditions.
